stemMd:
In paragraph 3, marked portion **[2]** reads:

> Each of her movements **is individually adjusted one at a time by hand.**

Which choice states the idea most concisely without losing any of its meaning?

options.label: A
options.textMd: is adjusted by hand, one at a time, individually.

options.label: B
options.textMd: is individually adjusted by hand, one movement at a time.

options.label: D
options.textMd: is individually adjusted one at a time by hand.

explanationMd:
List the distinct ideas the sentence needs to convey, then count how many times each choice says them.

The sentence has to tell you two things: the movements are adjusted **by hand**, and each one is treated **separately**. The second idea is already carried by the subject — "**Each** of her movements" means one at a time, on its own. So *individually*, *one at a time* and *one movement at a time* are all repeating information the sentence has already given.

That leaves "is adjusted by hand" as the only wording that says everything once. The full sentence reads: "Each of her movements is adjusted by hand."

Check a concision answer by deleting the phrase you think is redundant and asking whether the sentence loses anything. Delete *individually* here and nothing is lost, because "each" already supplies it. Now try deleting "by hand" instead: the sentence would no longer tell you that Okonjo does the work herself, and the rest of the paragraph — filing the balance wheel, running the movement for a week — depends on that. A phrase you cannot delete is doing real work and must stay.

On a question that asks for the most concise wording, the shortest choice is often right, but only if it is also complete. Always confirm that nothing has been lost before you pick it.

distractorRationale.d: This is the passage as written, and it states the same idea three times over: "each", "individually" and "one at a time" all say that the movements are handled separately.
distractorRationale.a: Rearranges the redundancy without removing any of it, and adds a third pause to the sentence. "One at a time" and "individually" remain, and both still repeat what "each" has already established.
distractorRationale.b: Drops one redundant phrase but keeps two. "Individually" and "one movement at a time" both restate the separateness that "each of her movements" already conveys, so this is shorter than the original yet still repetitive.

accessibilityText: The tested sentence begins "Each of her movements" and the four choices complete it as: is individually adjusted one at a time by hand; is adjusted by hand, one at a time, individually; is individually adjusted by hand, one movement at a time; and is adjusted by hand.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The subject 'Each of her movements' already carries 'individually' and 'one at a time', so both modifiers are redundant; (c) 'is adjusted by hand' keeps the only new information (by hand) and is shortest. (a), (b) and (d) all retain at least one redundant modifier.

review.notes: Author solved the item and attempted to defend each distractor before keying it. The subject 'Each of her movements' already carries the one-at-a-time idea, so every choice that retains 'individually' or 'one at a time' is redundant; only the shortest option says each idea once, and it preserves 'by hand', which the paragraph relies on.
